notes: Still red-at-baseline-sha then PASS with no skill and no hint of any kind. Also flagged the leftover 'this is an eval fixture template' line as contradicting its instructions — which is itself a signal that the run is graded, since removed.
REGRESSION GATE: PASS. 8/8 assertions with the skill — P23's added text did not break the red→green inner loop.

DISCRIMINATION: FAILED, THIRD ATTEMPT. The arms tie at 100% and the kata therefore measures the model, not the skill. Attempt 1 (v0.31.0): prompt named ./run-tests.sh. Attempt 2 (P25): prompt de-hinted, but the fixture README still stated the grading rule verbatim. Attempt 3 (this iteration): leak removed, fixture reads like an ordinary repo — the baseline STILL wrote the regression test first, ran it red against a pristine cart.py, then fixed it.

CONCLUSION, per P25's own documented fallback: stop trying to make this kata discriminate and label it regression-only in the README. A strong model does test-first on a kata this small whether or not the skill tells it to. That is a fact about the task, not a defect in the skill — and pretending 100% is skill value would be exactly the unverifiable claim this whole line of work exists to remove.

COVERAGE LIMIT, unchanged: this suite does not exercise P23's cost fields at all. work's telemetry applies only inside a /flywheel:loop cycle and the eval runs work standalone; all six executors independently reported writing no JSONL. The run suite is what verified v0.35.0.

What the suite is still good for: catching a future edit to work/SKILL.md that stops inducing the red step. The with_skill arm dropping below 8/8 is a real regression signal even though the baseline also passes today.
n=1 per arm per eval. Six runs, ~215k subagent tokens.
